author: Russell Brand
description:
A UFC fighter stepped to the microphone at the White House, praised Jesus Christ, thanked Trump for having the courage to host an event like this, and then told all of America that Michelle Obama is a man. Russell Brand asks the question the moment actually demands — are we able to locate truth within any of this, or is it all just bread and circuses dressed up as political courage? From the White House octagon to Candace Owens investigating Brigitte Macron, Russell unpacks why this wave of taboo-breaking commentary feels less like truth-telling and more like a new kind of performance — one that titillates without ever actually changing anything.

author: Russell Brand
description:
John McAfee laid it out with chilling clarity — the first thing any government needs to do is unify all of its data, healthcare records, genomic data, diagnostic data, into a single platform so it can be consumed by an AI model, and Russell Brand connects the dots to what is already happening with Oracle making large donations to Tony Blair's institute while Blair's institute advocates for Oracle's expansion across government data infrastructure. The centralization of data is the centralization of power, and McAfee's warning was that the technology exists today to criminalize anyone who becomes a problem to those in control. Digital ID, free speech laws, and the war against independent media are not separate issues — they are the same agenda moving in the same direction at the same time.

author: Russell Brand
description:
All it used to take was a meeting with the heads of the big newspapers and a quiet word with the BBC — this is what you say about vaccines, don't put anything else on. Russell Brand exposes the Trusted News Initiative, the organisation of mainstream media partners who quietly decided their real enemy was not each other but independent media, and reveals exactly why the British public stopped trusting the BBC, Channel 4, and every legacy outlet that claims to report the news. When you know they edit their material, when you know which side their bread is buttered, and when you know they coordinate against the very journalists trying to hold them accountable, the only remaining question is why anyone is still watching.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Bill Gates has openly admitted he probably has one of the highest greenhouse gas footprints of anyone on the planet, that his personal flying alone is gigantic, and that his solution is to pay a company $7 million a year to pull carbon out of the air and stick it underground. The same man pushing carbon limits on ordinary people, restructuring global food systems in the name of climate survival, and funding the transition away from meat and fossil fuels for the rest of humanity has decided that for himself, the offset is enough. Russell Brand lands the line that cuts through all of it — what are you going to do for the moral offset, Bill?

author: Russell Brand
description:
A 200-page report has exposed the most extensive and widespread scandal ever to beset Britain — babies abused, girls set on fire, testimonies beyond believable — and the British establishment that was supposed to protect its people singularly failed to investigate it, prosecute it, or answer for it. Russell Brand asks the question the report itself could not bring itself to fully answer: why would something this egregious, reported to police repeatedly, be dealt with through out-of-court disposals rather than prosecution? The law is not there to protect people. The law is a facility, a weapon, and a tool of the powerful — and occasionally a story breaks that makes that impossible to deny.
